blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: An asset has Weibull shape beta = 1.5. With the lesson's failure model, the value its renewal avoids is maximized as a function of renewal depth, on a five-point curve. How must that curve be written?

options.text: With segment variables only, since a maximized value needs no binaries
options.says: A maximized value needs no binaries only when its curve is concave; with beta below 2 the curve is convex.

options.text: With segment variables only, since every renewal curve is concave
options.says: Only assets with beta above 2 have concave curves; on GridCap small all five with beta below 2 were convex.

options.text: With one row per line, since the value falls with every quarter
options.says: The value rises with depth for every asset; and for a convex curve pushed up, rows under each line are not exact.

options.text: With binaries or bits, since its curve is convex and pushed up
options.says: Right: beta below 2 gives a convex curve, and a convex value pushed up needs the incremental, lambda or log form.

origin.section: Wearing-Out Assets Have Concave Curves, the Others Convex

questions.stem: An asset's true value curve is concave and the model uses its values at five depths, joined by straight lines. Between two of those depths, how does the model's value compare with the true one?

options.text: It is higher, since straight lines overrate every curve
options.says: A chord lies above a convex curve but below a concave one, so it does not overrate every curve.

options.text: It is lower, since a chord lies under a concave curve
options.says: Right: the five-point curve underrates concave assets between breakpoints, which is why the model's claim was below its plan's true value.

options.text: It is equal, since a concave curve leaves no gap
options.says: P019's concave curve had a worst gap of $30.3k with five breakpoints.

options.text: It is higher or lower by chance, set by the asset's age
options.says: The side is set by the shape: below for a concave curve, above for a convex one, at every age.

origin.section: Five Breakpoints Are an Approximation You Can Measure

questions.stem: A renewal model has six assets with concave value curves and four with convex ones, each curve with five breakpoints. Each curve is written as the lesson's renewal model chooses by shape. How many binaries do the curves add in all?

options.text: 30, three for each of the ten curves
options.says: That is the incremental form on every curve; the concave ones need no binaries when the value is pushed up.

options.text: 40, four for each of the ten curves
options.says: Four segments take three incremental binaries, one per segment but the last, and the concave curves take none.

options.text: 12, three for each of the four convex curves
options.says: Right: segments for the concave curves, the incremental form with K - 1 = 3 binaries for each convex one.

options.text: 0, since none of the ten curves is pushed down
options.says: A convex curve pushed up lets the solver skip to its steep segment, so it needs binaries.

origin.section: Each Curve Gets the Cheapest Exact Form
